1	import React from 'react';
2	import {
3	  Accordion,
4	  AccordionItem,
5	  AccordionButton,
6	  AccordionPanel,
7	  chakra,
8	  useMultiStyleConfig,
9	} from '@chakra-ui/react';
10	import { ChevronDownIcon, ChevronUpIcon } from 'app/components/icons';
11	
12	const ZIMM_ACCORDION_RECIPE = 'ZimmAccordion';
13	
14	export type ZimmAccordionItem = {
15	  /** Stable identifier — matches `defaultExpandedId` and acts as the React key. */
16	  id: string;
17	  /**
18	   * Group label shown in the header. Rendered uppercase via the `textStyle="productNames"`
19	   * design-system entry (see typography.ts), so callers pass Title Case ("Colour", not
20	   * "COLOUR") — this keeps i18n content faithful.
21	   */
22	  label: string;
23	  /**
24	   * Facet UI rendered inside the panel when expanded. SFCC-847 stops at the group
25	   * container — the real facet content (radio buttons, colour swatches, size chips, etc.)
26	   * is SFCC-108's scope.
27	   */
28	  content: React.ReactNode;
29	  /**
30	   * Optional content rendered directly under the header only when the item is collapsed —
31	   * use for a compact summary the shopper needs to see at a glance without expanding the
32	   * accordion (e.g. the current selection chips for a filter facet). Hidden when the item
33	   * is expanded so the full content in `content` takes over. Rendered outside Chakra's
34	   * AccordionPanel, so it does not participate in the expand/collapse animation.
35	   * Leave undefined for accordions with no summary.
36	   */
37	  alwaysVisibleContent?: React.ReactNode;
38	};
39	
40	type ZimmAccordionProps = {
41	  items: readonly ZimmAccordionItem[];
42	  /**
43	   * Which item is open on first render. Uncontrolled — the user can toggle from here on
44	   * without informing the parent.
45	   */
46	  defaultExpandedId?: string;
47	};
48	
49	/**
50	 * Single-open accordion group — a Zimmermann-styled wrapper around Chakra's Accordion
51	 * primitive. Delivers SFCC-847's accordion behaviour: only one item expanded at a time
52	 * (matches AC #5 and the DS 2026 Figma audited 2026-09-16, node
53	 * wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/40003890:151742 which shows exactly one accordion expanded),
54	 * expanding a new item collapses the previously expanded one, and each header exposes
55	 * `aria-expanded` reflecting its state (unchanged from Chakra's own `AccordionButton`).
56	 *
57	 * The chevron swaps ChevronDown (collapsed) ↔ ChevronUp (expanded) using the render-prop
58	 * form of `AccordionItem`. A CSS-only 180° rotation on a single glyph could animate
59	 * between them, but Zimmermann's own chevron pair (icons/zimm.tsx nodes 40002082:49961 and
60	 * 40002128:29217) are drawn as distinct shapes — swapping is faithful, rotating isn't.
61	 *
62	 * @param props see ZimmAccordionProps
63	 */
64	export const ZimmAccordion = ({ items, defaultExpandedId }: ZimmAccordionProps) => {
65	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_ACCORDION_RECIPE, {});
66	  // `findIndex` returns -1 when the id isn't in `items`. Chakra's `defaultIndex={-1}` logs a
67	  // "out of range" warning at dev-time; coercing to `undefined` instead falls back to
68	  // Chakra's own default (nothing expanded).
69	  const initialIndex = items.findIndex((item) => item.id === defaultExpandedId);
70	  const defaultIndex = initialIndex >= 0 ? initialIndex : undefined;
71	
72	  return (
73	    <Accordion allowToggle defaultIndex={defaultIndex} sx={styles.root}>
74	      {items.map((item) => (
75	        <AccordionItem key={item.id} sx={styles.item}>
76	          {({ isExpanded }) => (
77	            <>
78	              <AccordionButton sx={styles.header}>
79	                <chakra.span textStyle="productNames" sx={styles.label}>
80	                  {item.label}
81	                </chakra.span>
82	                {isExpanded ? (
83	                  <ChevronUpIcon boxSize="var(--zimm-icon-size-xl)" />
84	                ) : (
85	                  <ChevronDownIcon boxSize="var(--zimm-icon-size-xl)" />
86	                )}
87	              </AccordionButton>
88	              {!isExpanded && item.alwaysVisibleContent && (
89	                <chakra.div sx={styles.alwaysVisible}>{item.alwaysVisibleContent}</chakra.div>
90	              )}
91	              <AccordionPanel sx={styles.panel}>{item.content}</AccordionPanel>
92	            </>
93	          )}
94	        </AccordionItem>
95	      ))}
96	    </Accordion>
97	  );
98	};

content.text:
## Scale line

My brief named 5 priority items for one angle (correctness & regression) on an already-scoped PR review — not the full 10-angle standing set. I ran all 5, plus item 5's named "unrelated files" sweep. I did not fan out to sub-agents: the brief was already narrow enough (single angle, named files, named priority order) that further splitting would have added reconciliation overhead without shrinking the work. I did not touch styling/token/a11y-depth/story-interactivity/visual-checkpoint angles — those belong to whichever sibling angle is covering this PR's styling conformance, and a base-parity or Figma check would be someone else's lane, not mine. I re-ran (not re-used) `tsc --noEmit`, the full `vitest run`, and `eslint` scoped to the three priority files myself rather than trusting the numbers handed to me, since the brief asked me to.

---

## likely-defect

**1. 🔴 `resyncPendingRefine` is written, unit-tested, and never wired to the one caller its own docs say needs it — applying filters after browsing categories can silently drop the shopper's other filters.**
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525-529`:
```js
const handleCategoryChange = (id: string) => {
    if (id === pendingCategoryId) return;
    setPendingCategoryId(id);
    clearAll();
};
```
This only guards "clicked the same pending value twice." It never compares `id` to `categoryId` (the real, currently-applied category from the URL).

Concrete failure: shopper is on `/clothing/dresses` with `?refine=c_refinementColor=Black` already applied. They open the drawer (buffer resyncs to `pendingCategoryId="dresses"`, `pendingRefine={c_refinementColor:['Black']}`). They click "Tops" → `handleCategoryChange("tops")` → `clearAll()` fires, `pendingRefine={}`. They change their mind and click "Dresses" again → `handleCategoryChange("dresses")` → `"dresses" !== pendingCategoryId("tops")` → proceeds, `clearAll()` again (no-op, already empty). Now `pendingCategoryId === categoryId` (net category never really changed) but `pendingRefine` is still `{}`. They press APPLY → `buildAppliedRefine(searchParams.refine, managedAttributeIds, {})` (`useFilterDrawerState.ts:145-164`) deletes every managed attribute and writes nothing back → the shopper lands back on Dresses with their Black colour filter silently gone, despite never touching Colour.

`useFilterDrawerState.ts:31-36`'s own JSDoc names exactly this scenario as `resyncPendingRefine`'s reason to exist ("a caller that reverts a pending category change back to the currently-applied category... must also restore whatever refine is actually still applied"), and `useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81-95` unit-tests the function in isolation and passes. But `resyncPendingRefine` is destructured at `index.tsx:507` and never called again anywhere in the file (`grep -rn "resyncPendingRefine"` across the whole head worktree returns only the hook's own definition/JSDoc/test and this one unused destructure — confirmed, not just described). The category chip's own `onRemove` (`index.tsx:700-703`, `setPendingCategoryId(undefined); clearAll();`) doesn't call it either, and doesn't even match the test's own inline comment ("reverting it via the category chip's onRemove") — the chip clears to `undefined`, it doesn't revert to `categoryId`. Whichever UI action the author intended as the "revert" path, it isn't wired.
**CONFIRMED via full static trace** — every function in the chain (`handleCategoryChange`, `clearAll`, `buildAppliedRefine`) is pure and synchronous, so there's no runtime ambiguity; I did not click through a live app to watch it happen (no browser tool available to me), so treat "reproduced by execution" as not yet done. **ONE-OFF** in this PR, but the shape ("write and unit-test a fix function, forget to call it from production code, ship a green suite") is worth a broader grep if it recurs.

**2. 🔴 The "shop by store" filter (`StoreInventoryFilter` / `ilids`) has been dropped entirely, with no replacement and no acknowledgment anywhere in the diff.**
Base (`pr117-base/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:552-560, 717-720, 885-887`) renders `<StoreInventoryFilter toggleFilter={toggleFilter} selectedFilters={...} />` in both the desktop sidebar and the mobile filter modal, gated by `storeLocatorEnabled` (`config/default.js:44` sets this `true` by default — a genuinely live, on-by-default feature, also used by the header's store locator).
